clue.text: "Fats with everything": regime's starters sent back

parts.note: everything means all

indicators.note: sent back tells us to read the picked letters in the opposite direction
starters here are the opening letters of the word regime, its first two

explanation.surface: A quoted motto about having everything, followed by a regime turning its leaders away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' takes RE from regime and 'sent back' turns it to ER. Fats Waller was an American jazz pianist, which fits the puzzle's jazz theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Fats was the nickname of the jazz pianist and composer Thomas Waller.

clue.text: Don't expect it to look different in print, PC-wise

definitions.text: Don't expect it to look different in print, PC-wise

parts.words: Don't expect it to look different in print, PC-wise
parts.note: describes the computing acronym for 'what you see is what you get', a screen display matching the printed page

explanation.definitionFit: The acronym names an editor whose on-screen display matches the printed output exactly.

clue.text: One fat, round estate owner

indicators.note: round means the word for fat goes around the other piece

parts.note: lard is pig fat
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A portly, rotund landowner is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts I inside LARD. A laird is a Scottish landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a laird is the owner of a landed estate.

clue.text: Duke's wife out of footwear

indicators.note: out of tells us one piece is taken away from the footwear

parts.note: a wellington is a rubber boot

explanation.surface: A duke's spouse has kicked off her shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the Duke of Wellington, who gave his name to the boot; here Duke is Duke Ellington, the jazz bandleader. WELLINGTON loses W.
explanation.definitionFit: Duke was the nickname of the jazz composer and bandleader Edward Ellington.

clue.text: European nobleman put out of sight starts to act like gloomy outcast

parts.note: to put something out of sight is to hide it, past tense hid

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: An aristocrat goes into hiding and begins to behave like a gloomy pariah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes the first letters of act, like, gloomy, outcast, giving ALGO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a member of the lesser Spanish nobility, so a European noble.

clue.text: Feature of hedgehogs: kindling material!

indicators.note: Feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Hedgehog spines are offered as a source of fire-lighting material.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig leather is a material used for gloves, saddles and footballs.

clue.text: Miles from Victoria's entrance in middle of platform

indicators.note: in middle of places the letter inside the platform word

parts.note: a dais is a raised platform

indicators.note: entrance means the opening letter of Victoria

explanation.surface: A distance in miles from the entrance of Victoria station to the middle of a platform.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a railway station; Miles is the jazz trumpeter Miles Davis.
explanation.definitionFit: Miles is the first name of the jazz trumpeter Davis.

clue.text: Broken leg: rotten but held to improve vision

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's leg is broken and rotten but held up to make it better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges LEG and ROTTEN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorgnettes are spectacles held up to the eyes on a handle, so they improve sight.

clue.text: King Laurence lacks independence

indicators.note: lacks means the actor's surname is missing a letter

parts.note: Laurence Olivier was the famous English actor
I is the abbreviation for independence or independent

explanation.surface: An actor who played many kings is short of freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: OLIVIER without I. King Oliver was the jazz cornettist Joe 'King' Oliver.
explanation.definitionFit: King was the nickname of the New Orleans cornet player Joe Oliver.

clue.text: Woody Allen heartlessly pursuing Channel Island

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so this piece comes after the island

parts.note: Herm is one of the small Channel Islands

indicators.note: heartlessly strips out the insides of Allen, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Woody Allen chases someone onto a Channel Island.
explanation.walkthrough: Woody here is not Allen but Woody Herman, the jazz clarinettist and bandleader. Herm lies off Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody was the first name of the American big-band leader Herman.

clue.text: Film maker's pitch to another film maker (not male)

parts.note: a sales pitch is a spiel

indicators.note: not means the following piece is removed

parts.note: Ingmar Bergman was a Swedish film director
a man is a male

explanation.surface: One film director's sales talk to another director.
explanation.walkthrough: BERGMAN loses MAN to leave BERG.
explanation.definitionFit: Steven Spielberg is a celebrated Hollywood film director.

clue.text: Composer overdid "Ring" — date cut

indicators.note: cut means these letters are taken out of the word overdid

parts.note: a ring is O for its shape

explanation.surface: A composer went too far with the Ring cycle, so a performance date was cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O and the final D from OVERDID. 'Ring' tempts towards Wagner's cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was an Italian opera composer.

clue.text: Let out backward girl in congested city

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Great Wen is an old nickname for London, a wen being a swelling

indicators.note: backward means the girl's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A shy girl is let out into a crowded city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' reverses the girl's name before it goes in. William Cobbett called London 'the Great Wen', a wen being a swollen cyst.
explanation.definitionFit: To let out a garment is to widen it.

clue.text: What anagram of "seen" does to be rational!

parts.note: does here means produces or makes

indicators.note: anagram of tells us to rearrange the letters of the quoted word

explanation.surface: A puzzle asks what rearranging a word achieves.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging SEEN gives ENSE, so an anagram of seen 'makes ENSE'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rational or comprehensible is to be logical and coherent, an idiomatic phrase.

clue.text: Use it for film emulsion — back stage one can

indicators.note: back means the stage word is read in reverse

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
one gives A, the indefinite article
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Backstage, a crew member reaches for a can of film emulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LEG to GEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatin is the binding medium in photographic film emulsions.

clue.text: No score, therefore name G&S as crooner's speciality

parts.note: love means nil in tennis
so means therefore
the initials of Gilbert and Sullivan give G and S

explanation.surface: Without music, a singer names Gilbert and Sullivan as their specialism.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic ballads are a crooner's stock-in-trade.

clue.text: Make ineffective contribution to foundation, eg a tenner

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tenner donated to a charitable foundation achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate something is to cancel or nullify its effect.

clue.text: Dizzy spell — collapsed when hugged by soldier, that is

indicators.note: hugged by means the jumbled letters sit inside the outer pieces

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

indicators.note: collapsed signals the letters of spell are jumbled

parts.note: the word spell is the fodder

explanation.surface: A soldier holds someone who fainted in a dizzy spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' jumbles spell; 'hugged by' sets it between the soldier and 'that is'. Dizzy here is the bebop trumpeter, not light-headedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Dizzy was the nickname of the bebop trumpeter John Birks Gillespie.

clue.text: Still awake? Then get level

parts.note: still means even, as in 'even more'
up means out of bed and awake

explanation.surface: A question about being awake, then an instruction to settle a score.
explanation.definitionFit: To square things or make them equal is to get level.

clue.text: Abbot, rather too holy on the outside, heading a former European state

indicators.note: heading means this assembly comes before the letter A
on the outside means the holy word wraps round the comedian's name

parts.note: pi is slang for sanctimonious or excessively pious
Russ Abbot is a British comedian, so Abbot leads to Russ

explanation.surface: An overly pious abbot leads a former European country.
explanation.walkthrough: Russ Abbot is a British TV comedian, though 'Abbot' looks like a monk. 'heading' puts the wrapped piece before A.
explanation.definitionFit: Prussia was a German kingdom and state, abolished after the Second World War.

clue.text: Go through life again accepting end of life of ease

indicators.note: accepting means the first piece takes in the letter

parts.note: to relive is to experience life a second time

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the second life

explanation.surface: Living one's life again in comfort and leisure.
explanation.walkthrough: E, the end of 'life', goes inside RELIVE. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve pain or worry is to ease it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Jimmy's jocular follower, a bit of a poser?

definitions.meaning: in rhyming slang 'jimmy ...' means a piddle, so the word follows Jimmy in that joke phrase
a poser is a puzzling question, a conundrum

explanation.walkthrough: Rhyming slang is Cockney: a word replaced by a phrase that rhymes with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum or puzzling question is a poser; the second word of the slang phrase follows Jimmy.

clue.text: Train old partner to iron

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Someone trains their former spouse to do the ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: An express is a fast train with few stops.

clue.text: We hear Sydney harbour's centre etc he redeveloped

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letter of harbour
redeveloped signals that etc and he are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sydney Harbour's centre has been redeveloped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear Sydney' points to Sidney, spelt differently: the clarinettist Sidney Bechet. B from harbour's middle, then ETC HE rearranged gives ECHET.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidney Bechet was a New Orleans saxophonist; the spoken name sounds the same as Sydney.

clue.text: On the tube to Upminster, unlike the young man who accepted pioneering advice?

definitions.text: On the tube to Upminster, unlike the young man who accepted pioneering advice?

parts.words: On the tube to Upminster, unlike the young man who accepted pioneering advice?
parts.note: Upminster is at the eastern end of the London Underground District line; 'Go west, young man' was the advice to American pioneers

explanation.definitionFit: Travelling towards the east, the opposite of the westward pioneer journey.

clue.text: Count on Brummie being admitted to foundation

indicators.note: being admitted to means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a base is a foundation
Brummie is the setter, who refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: Relying on a Birmingham native joining the founding body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link. Count Basie was the jazz bandleader; a Brummie is someone from Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: Count was the title-like nickname of the bandleader William Basie.

clue.text: Drugs kill — and hinder in legal terms

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so ES is drugs
top is slang for kill

explanation.surface: Drugs are lethal and a legal obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: Estop is a legal term meaning to bar or preclude someone from asserting something.

clue.text: Art's voluntary fighters taking on corporation

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
corporation is jocular slang for a large belly, a tum

explanation.surface: The army reserve recruits a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: Art Tatum was a jazz pianist; 'taking on' joins the pieces. Corporation as a paunch is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Tatum was a virtuoso jazz pianist, so his surname completes the name.

clue.text: Earl performs well, topless

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: someone who shines performs brilliantly

explanation.surface: An aristocrat excels despite being half undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Earl Hines was a jazz pianist; Earl is not a nobleman here.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl was the first name of the jazz pianist Hines.

clue.text: Tar baby has Remus' back problem eliminated with fertiliser

parts.note: a tar or salt is a sailor
a pet is a darling, a baby

indicators.note: eliminated means those letters are removed from Remus
back means the problem word is read in reverse

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: The Tar-Baby story is told with Uncle Remus's back trouble cured by fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: SUM turned back gives MUS, which is eliminated from REMUS to leave RE. The surface evokes the Uncle Remus tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is used as a fertiliser.

clue.text: Hardy character with period marble piece?

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine
an era is a period

explanation.surface: A Hardy heroine is linked to a period of marble sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is a small tile of marble or glass used in mosaic.

clue.text: Mercury component of isotherm escalation

indicators.note: component of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Mercury rises as temperature lines climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is the Roman counterpart of Hermes, messenger of the Greek gods.
